changes: Implements section 1 of docs/requirements/decisions/red-evidence-subsystem-spec.md: the assertion envelope that makes WHAT a RED run asserted machine-checkable, instead of self-reported. Today redEvidenceRecordSatisfied only checks that a record claims a non-empty observed failure, so a fabricated or vacuous RED satisfies the gate. packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts is the bulk: it validates the envelope schema with matcher ids unique per envelope and kind restricted to the closed set {literal-line, class} with NO pattern language, enforces the closed stream/polarity/expectedExitClass enums, requires at least one present-in-red matcher and allows greenExempt only on that polarity, rejects the timeout-is-failure-with-script-exit linkage at schema time, validates supplementaryArtifact path syntax, computes assertionDigest and refuses a declared digest that does not recompute. packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/specificity.ts implements the minimum-specificity rule: rule 1 rejects blocklisted catch-alls, and rule 2 is a length AND entropy CONJUNCTION, not a disjunction. packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts exposes it as the READ-ONLY command red_evidence_envelope_check, wired into command-catalog, command-policy, process-fact-levels, activity-policy and registry. Five committed RED harnesses ship and are registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands: red-w2d-rejection-matrix (142 fixtures, tags R1-1/2/3/5/6), red-w2d-specificity-conjunction, red-w2d-command-readonly, red-w2d-assertion-digest-scope, red-w2d-entropy-differential, plus the task smoke red-evidence-envelope-smoke (33 tagged rejection fixtures). Three further commits came out of review rather than from the implementer: 19aeb9de6f removed a 'do not re-litigate' directive from the source and corrected the argument it defended; 77a5ffab9e made the first-run precondition failure name WHERE to set the policy; 90c21f7f4d added a characterization fixture pinning the specificity metric's behaviour on short real-world constants.
usage: proof-or-stop red_evidence_envelope_check --storyId=<id> --assertionFile=<path.json> [--json]. It is read-only and writes no chain record: it validates a CANDIDATE envelope and reports admissibility plus the computed assertionDigest BEFORE a RED run is spent, so a malformed or under-specified assertion is caught without burning an execution. The candidate may omit policyDigest and assertionDigest (computing the latter is the command's purpose); if either IS supplied it must equal the computed value or the envelope is inadmissible with a named diagnostic. The command requires a resolved red-evidence policy; with none configured it fails closed and now tells the operator where to fix it: 'red_evidence_policy_missing: pinnedPath' followed by 'Set these under the "redEvidence" block in lattice.config.json at the project root; run proof-or-stop doctor to see the resolved red-evidence policy.'
expectedOutcome: An operator can submit a candidate assertion envelope and learn, before spending a RED run, whether it is admissible and WHY it is not: each rejection carries its §1.6 tag and a human-readable reason naming the exact value and the exact numbers that failed. An over-broad matcher cannot be admitted: there is no regex language to write one in, degenerate literals are blocklisted, and a value must clear both a length and an entropy floor. The command writes nothing.
actualTranscript: Executed by four reviewer lanes and a cross-vendor codex host independently. A real rejection reads: '[R1-2] matcher-below-specificity-floor: matcher m1: value "SIGSEGV" fails the §1.3 rule 2 CONJUNCTION (length floor AND entropy floor, both inclusive) - len=7 < minMatcherLen=8; entropyBits=15.65 < minMatcherEntropyBits=24' and '[R1-1] target-exercised-proof-absent: assertion.targetExercisedProof is absent or is not an object (§1.6 R1-1): a RED that cannot prove it exercised the named acceptance target cannot satisfy the gate'. With no policy configured the command exits 1 printing the missing key AND the file and block to set it in, plus a doctor pointer; a wrong-SHAPE guess produces a second, more specific diagnostic, so a newcomer is unblocked within two attempts. The read-only claim is proven mechanically, not asserted: red-w2d-command-readonly uses a positive git-only spawn allowlist and a .lattice content-hash manifest that is byte-identical before and after a batch of direct handler invocations. Full validate: 111 of 111 commands pass, verification coverage 108 of 108 fresh with zero gaps.
outcomeDiff: No difference on what section 1 asked for; the envelope, the matcher admissibility layer, the specificity rule and the read-only command are all delivered and all covered by registered regressions. What this story DID NOT do, and did not claim to: it does not retire the v1 surface. red_evidence_create and redEvidenceRecordSatisfied are untouched - packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts has zero diff from the merge base - and command-catalog still lists red_evidence_create alongside the new command with no superseded language, which is correct because retirement is section 6's adoption point, not this leaf's. Five defects this story PROVED remain open, each one DISCOVERED during the work and absent from the original normalizedOutcome and acceptanceClaim, so none of them is a promise this story retracted; each now has a real owner rather than a sentence: B-595c holds the three-site matcher-value bounds contradiction (F-051/F-054), the missing candidate-envelope schema (F-052), the inverted specificity metric (F-058) and the undocumented exit-class canonical form (F-050); B-3654 holds a command documented as append-nothing that appends an activity-log row (F-014). Both were created only after the concept lane established in F-064 that five resolution records had claimed 'filed as follow-up' when nothing had been filed.
limitations: The specificity metric is inverted on a nameable class of real input and this story ships it that way. Measured: SIGSEGV (7 bytes, 15.65 bits), ENOMEM (6, 11.51), HTTP 404 (8, 20.00) and Error 500 (9, 21.77) are all REJECTED, while the vaguer phrase 'test failed' (11, 34.05) is ADMITTED - because character-level Shannon entropy measures alphabet diversity, not semantic specificity, so short well-known constants score below longer generic English. ENOMEM sits below the NON-TUNABLE 12-bit hard floor, so no policy can ever admit it: a RED assertion can never pin on ENOMEM. This is NOT a soundness break - R1-4 independently requires every present-in-red matcher to have matched the actual RED output, so an admitted vague literal still cannot make a fabricated RED satisfiable, and greenExempt waives only the absent-at-GREEN conjunct per-matcher - but it is a real usability limit: an operator whose failure signature is a short constant must pad it with surrounding line text. The current behaviour is pinned by a characterization fixture so that changing the formula fails mechanically; the fixture is explicitly not an endorsement. The spec and the code also disagree in three places about whether matcher-value bounds apply to class values: §1.1.1 scopes them to literal-line, §1.6 R1-3 bounds any matcher value, §1.2 restates it unqualified. Two of those are normative and they contradict each other; the code implements the §1.1.1 reading and which reading SHOULD win is open. Separately, the spec never describes the candidate-envelope schema this command validates, so the implementation's most load-bearing scope decision is documented only in a source comment. Both are B-595c's.
pitfalls: Three worth carrying. FIRST, and it is the headline, stated WITHOUT a count because three attempts to attach one were each false and each caught by a reviewer (B-9ff1:F-066, F-067, F-068, F-069): the reviewer lane whose job was auditing the story owner's STATEMENTS about the code found defects there repeatedly, in a story whose code was in good shape, and none of those defects was self-caught. Re-derive rather than trust a restatement - grouping findings.json on createdAt and grepping resolvedReason for a cited commit shows twenty findings filed on 2026-08-18 across four lanes, four of them citing a source commit, so 'all prose, zero code findings' was false at every width I tried it. The shape repeated - claiming a verification that was not performed, then claiming it again inside the correction. 'Verified independently' had checked one of two locations. A correction said it was 'appended' when finding_resolve --resolution is a plain overwrite. The replacement 'verbatim' block was a retyping that silently dropped 377 of 1216 bytes, including the original's own honesty caveat - caught by a difflib diff whose shape (three scattered deletions plus an em-dash/hyphen substitution) proved retyping rather than truncation. Five records said 'filed as follow-up' with nothing filed. A correction to F-058 was written into F-062 instead of F-058, which is the record the follow-up story cites. The rule that came out of it: before writing any sentence about verification, ownership or tool behaviour into an audit record, run the one command that would falsify it - every time, the reviewer ran that command and the author had not. SECOND, reviewers must decline to record a pass while a blocking finding is open; the concept lane did this three times and it is the only reason this story did not close on false records. Ask each lane the question only it can answer: the behavior lane found the specificity inversion by being asked whether the rule rejects what it should NOT, the inverse of what every other lane was asking. THIRD, mechanics. A cross-host quorum binds storyFilesHash, not the whole tree: merging 41 commits of other stories left fullQuorum 3/3 intact via drift-accept, and a whole four-lane round was run here on the false premise that the quorum had died - reviewer Prompt Envelopes are a SEPARATE binding that does go stale on a merge. story_advance carries a flat 900000ms watchdog that a 111-command validate now exceeds at command 40; the route through is a standalone validate under a raised LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS producing a stored PASS the gate then reuses, and that variable must never be set on a gate command because it is baked into effectiveEnvironmentDigest. verification_evidence_batch_add executes its pinned commands serially against a 300s no-output watchdog, so a 108-record batch aborts; batch by five.
